column1: # LONGER SCHEDULE on the three bases: 60 epochs (was 30), eta_min 1e-5 (was 1e-7).
# User direction 2026-09-20: "curious how it would perform in comparison".
# WHAT IS VARIED: the LR schedule only -- epochs 30 -> 60 and the cosine floor 1e-7 -> 1e-5,
# both passed as overrides so every loss term is bit-identical to the 30-epoch original.
# HELD FIXED per arm, exactly as the base: E1 = M03 (dcos 0.01, no mag, no latent);
# Everything else is arm s313: adjacency_map, batch 2048, lr 1e-3, decoder_lr 1e-3,
# cosine_loss_weight 0.5, film multiplicative_only, fh 256, mean-free, seed 42.
# ⚠️ eta_min 1e-5 is 100x HIGHER than the current 1e-7, so the run ends at a much larger
# learning rate rather than annealing to near-zero. Combined with 2x the epochs this is a
# genuinely different optimisation, not just "more of the same" -- it may help by escaping a
# sharp minimum, or hurt by never settling.
# READ AGAINST (test, uncalibrated, 5/5, 30 epochs / eta_min 1e-7):
# ANCHORS: meanpert 0.1324 · transfer 0.2323 · experimental 0.3722 (mae 0.0257).
# `mae` is an ERROR: LOWER IS BETTER.
# PRE-REGISTERED. All three improve -> the 30-epoch schedule was undertrained and every prior
# comparison was made at a suboptimal stopping point. Mixed -> the schedule interacts with the
# loss composition, so schedule and loss cannot be tuned independently. All three degrade ->
# 30 epochs with a near-zero floor was already right, and the extra compute buys nothing.
# ⚠️ Epoch count also changes WHICH checkpoint `best_model.pth` is: these arms select over 60
# epochs, the originals over 30. A gain could be a better optimum OR simply more chances to
# catch the validation metric's known +/-0.20 inter-epoch oscillation (F7).
